You are a data modelling expert who classifies database tables as "fact", "dimension", "bridge", or "reference".

You receive:
  1. The full database schema with column and FK details.
  2. Heuristic pre-classifications from FK graph analysis (use as a prior, not ground truth).
  3. Business context (industry, metrics, goals).

Your job is to validate the heuristic results, correct misclassifications, and assign a confidence
score (1–3) to each table. Set needs_clarification=True for tables where you are genuinely unsure.

Definitions:
  - FACT: Records a business event or transaction. Has a date column + measures (quantities, amounts,
    rates) + FKs to dimensions. Examples: order_details, orders, transactions, events, sessions.
  - DIMENSION: Describes a business entity. Has many descriptive text/categorical attributes. May have
    outgoing FKs to other dimensions (snowflake). Examples: customers, products, employees, categories.
  - BRIDGE: Resolves a many-to-many relationship. Has ONLY two FK columns (+ maybe a surrogate key)
    and almost NO other attributes. Examples: employee_territories, user_roles, product_tags.
  - REFERENCE: Small standalone lookup table with no FKs in or out. Examples: us_states, currencies,
    status_codes, country_codes.

Critical rules — override heuristics when these apply:
  1. A PRODUCT/ITEM CATALOG is always a DIMENSION, even if it has outgoing FKs to categories or
     suppliers. Having outgoing FKs to lookup tables = snowflake pattern, not a fact.
  2. An EMPLOYEE or PERSON table is always a DIMENSION, even with a self-referencing FK (reports_to)
     or outgoing FKs to a region/department table.
  3. A true BRIDGE has almost no columns beyond its two FK columns. If a table has 3+ non-FK
     descriptive attributes (names, descriptions, amounts), it is a DIMENSION or FACT, not a bridge.
  4. FACTS always have at least one numeric measure column AND a transaction date column.
     "Header" tables (e.g. salesorderheader, purchaseorderheader) ARE facts — they record a
     business transaction event with a date and monetary amounts. Association tables with NO
     numeric measures and NO transaction date are BRIDGE, not fact.
  5. Reference/lookup tables (e.g. us_states, region) with no transactional data are REFERENCE.

Examples (Northwind-style schema):
  order_details(order_id→orders, product_id→products, unit_price, quantity, discount) → FACT
    reason: has measures + FKs to dimensions, records order line events
  products(product_id, product_name, category_id→categories, supplier_id→suppliers, unit_price) → DIMENSION
    reason: entity descriptor; outgoing FKs to lookup tables = snowflake, not a fact
  employees(employee_id, name, hire_date, reports_to→employees) → DIMENSION
    reason: entity descriptor; self-referencing FK does not make it a fact or bridge
  employee_territories(employee_id→employees, territory_id→territories) → BRIDGE
    reason: exactly 2 FK columns, no descriptive attributes, resolves many-to-many
  us_states(state_id, state_name, region_id) → REFERENCE
    reason: small static lookup with no transactional data

Output format: keep each `reasoning` to ≤8 words.

Database schema:
  product_categories(id, name, parent_category_id→product_categories, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  products(id, sku, name, description, category_id→product_categories, unit_of_measure, weight_kg, standard_cost, sale_price, lead_time_days, reorder_point, status, created_at, updated_at)
  raw_materials(id, code, name, description, unit_of_measure, weight_kg, standard_cost, reorder_point, minimum_order_quantity, lead_time_days, hazardous, status, created_at, updated_at)
  bill_of_materials(id, product_id→products, version, description, base_quantity, unit_of_measure, is_active, effective_from, effective_to, created_by, created_at, updated_at)
  bom_items(id, bom_id→bill_of_materials, raw_material_id→raw_materials, component_product_id→products, quantity, unit_of_measure, scrap_percentage, sequence_number, notes)
  suppliers(id, code, name, contact_name, email, phone, address_line1, address_line2, city, state_province, postal_code, country, payment_terms_days, currency, rating, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  purchase_orders(id, po_number, supplier_id→suppliers, order_date, expected_delivery_date, actual_delivery_date, status, currency, exchange_rate, subtotal, tax_amount, total_amount, notes, created_by, created_at, updated_at)
  purchase_order_items(id, purchase_order_id→purchase_orders, raw_material_id→raw_materials, quantity_ordered, quantity_received, unit_cost, line_total, expected_delivery_date, notes)
  warehouses(id, code, name, address_line1, address_line2, city, state_province, postal_code, country, manager_name, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  stock_locations(id, warehouse_id→warehouses, code, name, aisle, rack, shelf, bin, max_capacity, location_type, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  inventory(id, stock_location_id→stock_locations, product_id→products, raw_material_id→raw_materials, quantity_on_hand, quantity_reserved, quantity_available, lot_number, serial_number, expiry_date, unit_cost, last_counted_at, created_at, updated_at)
  cost_centers(id, code, name, description, parent_cost_center_id→cost_centers, budget, actual_cost, fiscal_year, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  work_centers(id, code, name, description, cost_center_id→cost_centers, warehouse_id→warehouses, capacity_per_hour, labor_cost_per_hour, machine_cost_per_hour, overhead_cost_per_hour, efficiency_percentage, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  operations(id, code, name, description, default_work_center_id→work_centers, standard_duration_hours, setup_time_hours, operation_type, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  routing(id, product_id→products, operation_id→operations, work_center_id→work_centers, sequence_number, standard_duration_hours, setup_time_hours, labor_cost_per_hour, machine_cost_per_hour, notes, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  production_orders(id, order_number, product_id→products, bom_id→bill_of_materials, work_center_id→work_centers, planned_quantity, produced_quantity, rejected_quantity, planned_start_date, planned_end_date, actual_start_date, actual_end_date, status, priority, cost_center_id→cost_centers, estimated_cost, actual_cost, output_location_id→stock_locations, notes, created_by, created_at, updated_at)
  production_order_items(id, production_order_id→production_orders, raw_material_id→raw_materials, component_product_id→products, inventory_id→inventory, required_quantity, issued_quantity, returned_quantity, unit_of_measure, unit_cost, line_total, notes)
  quality_checks(id, production_order_id→production_orders, check_date, checked_by, quantity_inspected, quantity_passed, quantity_failed, result, inspection_type, notes, created_at, updated_at)

Heuristic pre-classifications:
  product_categories: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 1 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  products: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  raw_materials: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  bill_of_materials: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  bom_items: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 3 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  suppliers: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  purchase_orders: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  purchase_order_items: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  warehouses: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  stock_locations: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  inventory: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  cost_centers: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  work_centers: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  operations: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  routing: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  production_orders: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  production_order_items: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 4 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  quality_checks: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.

Business context: Database "manufacturing". Domain inferred from table/column names.
